content: Citral, also known as 3,7-dimethyl-2,6-octadienal or lemonal, is a compound that exists as two terpenoid isomers with the molecular formula C10H16O. These two isomers differ in the configuration of their double bonds. The trans isomer is referred to as geranial or citral A, while the cis isomer is called neral or citral B. Geranial is characterized by a strong lemon-like odor, whereas neral has a less intense but sweeter lemon scent. Due to its distinct citrus aroma, citral is widely utilized in the perfume industry to impart a fresh, lemony fragrance. It is also employed as a flavoring agent and as an additive to enhance the properties of lemon oil. Beyond its sensory applications, citral exhibits potent antimicrobial properties and has been observed to influence pheromonal activity in insects. In industrial chemistry, citral serves as a precursor in the synthesis of vitamin A, as well as ionone and methylionone, which are compounds used in the production of fragrances and flavors. Citral is naturally found in significant concentrations in the essential oils of various plants, including lemon myrtle (90-95%), Litsea cubeba (70-85%), lemongrass (65-85%), lemon verbena (30-35%), lemon balm, and citrus fruits such as lemons and oranges.
